title: api-gateway: tune routing rules, streaming proxy buffers, and payload size limits for OpenAI-compat stability
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: customers have reported intermittent streaming stalls and truncated structured output when requests are routed through the API gateway to the streaming proxy (particularly under high-concurrency bursts and when using the OpenAI-compat path). This PR adjusts routing heuristics, raises the streaming proxy per-connection buffer limits, and tightens payload size enforcement to improve stability and predictable behavior across hosted and dedicated deployments. Changes include: 1) add per-route routing policy overrides so latency-sensitive routes (chat/stream and function-calling) prefer low-concurrency pools and bypass multi-tenant batching when request size exceeds configured thresholds; 2) increase streaming-proxy in-memory buffer from 64KB->256KB with backpressure signaling to avoid mid-response truncation of chunked JSON (structured output) while retaining overall memory caps; 3) introduce explicit payload-size rejections at the gateway (413-like behavior) for requests that exceed model- and route-specific limits to avoid upstream plumbing errors; 4) OpenAI-compat shim: ensure chunk delimiters and content-length semantics are preserved by the proxy, add tests for function-calling tool payloads and structured JSON sequences. Checklist: [x] unit tests for routing policy logic [x] integration test against streaming-proxy [x] e2e regression test using openai-compat example app [x] docs update for default payload limits (console + docs site) Related: ENG-5123 (stability), ENG-5231 (openai-compat structured-output regressions).

review_conversation: Aisha Patel (reviewer): Can we make the 256KB buffer configurable per deployment? Some on-prem customers have tighter memory budgets.
Maya Chen (author): Yes, added max_connection_mem and per-route caps in streaming-proxy/config.toml. Default remains 256KB for hosted to reduce regressions; on-prem operators can tune downward.
Diego Marquez (reviewer): The payload rejection path needs a clear error contract for OpenAI-compat clients so they see a 413-like error. Add tests and docs.
Maya Chen (author): Added explicit 413-style JSON error body for OpenAI-compat responses and included e2e test in tests/integration.
Evan Roberts (reviewer): Concern: bypassing batching for certain routes impacts cost/perf — add metrics to monitor batching bypass rate and fallback to standard path on pressure.
Maya Chen (author): Added counters: gateway.routing.bypass.count and gateway.routing.bypass.fallback.count; added automatic fallback when low-concurrency pools are saturated.
Aisha Patel: LGTM after minor nits fixed.
notes: Behavioral impact: default behavior is backward-compatible for most routes but streaming stability for chat/stream and function-calling routes is improved. Some high-payload requests will now be rejected at gateway rather than forwarded and failing downstream; this is intentional to provide clearer errors to clients.

Monitoring: new metrics added (gateway.routing.bypass.count, gateway.routing.bypass.fallback.count, streaming_proxy.connection.buffer_utilization). Recommend creating a console alert if bypass.fallback rate > 5% over 5m.
Rollback plan: revert feature flag (route-policy-v2) and config changes; streaming-proxy buffer can be rolled back to 64KB quickly via config change without code revert.
release_notes: Improved streaming stability for chat/stream and function-calling routes by tuning gateway routing and streaming-proxy buffers
Gateway will now enforce route- and model-specific payload limits with clearer 413-style errors for OpenAI-compat clients
Added per-route overrides in Console to prefer low-concurrency pools for latency-sensitive routes
Monitoring: new metrics for routing bypass and streaming-proxy buffer utilization
changelog_entry: Tuned API gateway routing heuristics and streaming-proxy buffers to improve streaming stability and OpenAI-compat structured output behavior; added payload-size enforcement and per-route overrides.
example_request_changes: Previously large streaming request with embedded tool-calling payloads could be forwarded and cause upstream truncation; gateway now rejects requests over route.payload_limit with immediate 413-like JSON error.
OpenAI-compat streaming now preserves chunk delimiters and content-length semantics; example clients should see consistent streaming frames.
security_considerations: No new secrets. Increased in-memory buffer requires monitoring on on-prem installs; documented max_connection_mem and per-route caps.
